If B is exactly invertible, solve B^T*lambda=e_ankle exactly. Then x_ankle=lambda^T*e-lambda^T*h-lambda^T*G*v. This is a new adjoint right-hand side, not the completed correction or a saved rejected direction.
For verified outer native-coordinate bounds L_j<=v_j<=U_j, define S=sum_j max(-(lambda^T*G)_j*L_j,-(lambda^T*G)_j*U_j). Thus x_ankle<=t*sum|lambda|-lambda^T*h+S.

Combining gives t>=(lambda^T*h-S-m)/sum|lambda|, when sum|lambda|>0. A bound strictly above a specified progress threshold could rule out that threshold for the full current linearized problem. It would not prove physical impossibility or produce an admissible motion.

A checker could verify a nonnegative combination of the actual original ankle, signed-consistency and singleton interval rows, eliminating every native direction coordinate. The resulting scalar inequality is necessary for every feasible full-original point.
